Abstract

1 Reinforcement learning has gathered much attention in recent years due to its rapid   
2 development and rich applications, especially on control systems and robotics.   
3 When tackling real-world applications with reinforcement learning method, the   
4 corresponded Markov decision process may have huge discrete or even continuous   
5 state/action space. Deep reinforcement learning has been studied for handling these   
6 issues through deep learning for years, and one promising branch is the actor-critic   
7 architecture. Many past studies leveraged multiple critics to enhance the accuracy   
8 of evaluation of a policy for addressing the overestimation and underestimation   
9 issues. However, few studies have considered the architecture with multiple actors   
10 together with multiple critics. This study proposes a novel multi-actor multi-critic   
11 (MAMC) deep deterministic reinforcement learning method. The proposed method   
12 has three main features, including selection of actors based on non-dominated   
13 sorting for exploration with respect to skill and creativity factors, evaluation for   
14 actors and critics using a quantile-based ensemble strategy, and exploiting actors   
15 with best skill factor. Theoretical analysis proves the learning stability and bounded   
16 estimation bias for the MAMC. The present study examines the performance on   
17 a well-known reinforcement learning benchmark MuJoCo. Experimental results   
18 show that the proposed framework outperforms state-of-the-art deep deterministic   
19 based reinforcement learning methods. Experimental analysis also indicates the   
20 proposed components are effective. Empirical analysis further investigates the   
21 validity of the proposed method, and shows its benefit on complicated problems.
22 1 Introduction

23 Reinforcement learning (RL) has been studied for decades that is proved powerful when dealing   
24 with problems and applications which is assumed or is able to be formulated as a Markov decision   
25 process [25]. Numerous applications have been successfully solved by RL methods such as playing   
26 board games [26], training large-language model [24], and controlling humanoid [29]. RL methods   
27 are of several types, including value-based approach, policy gradient approach, policy optimization   
28 approach, and actor-critic approach [28]. This study focus on actor-critic based RL methods due to   
29 its nice performance on continuous control problems.   
30 A common issue in RL is the huge or infinite space of states/actions, making conventional tabular   
31 methods inapplicable, and a straight forward solution is to construct approximation function for   
32 space transformation. As the rapid growth in high performance computing and deep learning [3],   
33 leveraging deep learning for building mapping function in RL methods, forming deep reinforcement   
34 learning (DRL), becomes possible. One representative method of DRL is the deep Q-learning (DQN)   
35 [23], which adopted deep convolution neural network to estimate the state-action function (a.k.a. $Q$   
36 function).   
37 Advanced issues in deep reinforcement learning have been studied and investigated in past years   
38 [11]. Essential issues covers learning stability [2, 19, 9], estimation accuracy for handling issues of   
39 overestimation [4, 20], underestimation [7, 35] or both [32, 1, 15], sampling efficiency [10, 36, 22? ],   
40 ensemble learning [21, 6, 16, 14, 34] and so forth, and hybridization of components for addressing   
41 these issues is proved to gain effectiveness and learning efficiency [12]. It is worth noting that   
42 these issues are highly correlated so that ensemble learning could handle estimation accuracy, which   
43 may bring learning stability and sampling efficiency, and thus results in better performance and   
44 convergence.   
45 This study proposes a novel method: multiple-actors-multiple-critics (MAMC) deep deterministic   
46 reinforcement learning to address the above issues. The main features of the MAMC are threefold:   
47 1) The MAMC manipulates multiple actors and critics in a current manner without predetermined   
48 relations, 2) The MAMC evaluates actors and critics as per a quantile-based ensemble strategy, and   
49 3) The MAMC selects actors for exploration in learning on the basis of non-dominated sorting with   
50 respect to skill and creativity factors. The emerging MAMC is capable of facilitating nice exploration   
51 among multiple actors in the meantime improving and smoothing the learning of critics, which is key   
52 to stabilize the guiding force to actors.

• Devise a parametric quantile-based ensemble estimator considering multiple actors and multiple critics for the target values of critics learning   
• Design an actor evaluation and selection approach based on skill and creativity factors for exploration and exploitation   
• Theoretically prove the MAMC has stable learning and bounded estimation bias   
• Empirically examine the quality and validity of the MAMC, and investigate the run-time behavior of MAMC by inspecting into the proposed components

65 2 Related Work

66 The actor-critic architecture is proposed by Konda and Tsitsiklis [13]. Table 1 compiles six out nine   
67 categories of actor-critic architectures in terms of the number of actors and critics for some recent   
68 proposed actor-critic-based RL methods. To the best of our knowledge, it is merely no study for   
69 actor-critic architectures with fewer number of actors than of critics.   
70 SASC. For single-actor single-critic (SASC) architecture, a representative study is the deep Q  
71 network (DQN) [23], which introduced deep convolution neural network into RL and brought nice   
72 performance on Atari. Another famous SASC-based method is the deep deterministic policy gradient   
73 (DDPG) [19]. DDPG ameliorated the learning stability and efficiency of DQN by combining deep   
74 learning with policy gradient for solving control problems with continuous action space.   
75 SADC. Beyond SASC, lots of methods are proposed with a single actor and double critics, noted   
76 as SADC, for solving the issues of overestimation and exploration. In [9], a twin delayed deep   
77 deterministic policy gradient (TD3) was proposed. TD3 improved DDPG by adopting two critic   
78 networks, where a minimum of the corresponded two target networks are served as the computa  
79 tional basis of target value. TD3 also proposed the delayed update of actor, i.e., a lower update   
80 frequency than critics, for stabilizing the learning of the actor. Soft Actor-Critic (SAC) considered   
81 stochastic policy and introduced soft value function for training the two critics of soft Q-function   
82 [10]. Specifically, SAC trained a stochastic policy network to transform noise to an action for a given   
83 state as condition, and the training depends on a policy gradient for maximizing the randomness of   
84 the resulting actions, and the approximated Q values obtained from the minimum of the two critics   
85 as TD3. Different from TD3, SAC trained the two critics independently according to the target soft   
86 value function network, which is soft-updated by the soft value function network, while the soft   
87 value function network is trained by minimizing the different to the target value, which is calculated   
88 as the expectation of state-action value of the minimum of the two critics over action given by the   
89 actor. Optimistic Actor-Critic (OAC) further pointed out the issues of inefficient exploration owing   
90 to insufficient pessimistic in TD3 and SAC, and proposed an amelioration to guide the exploration   
91 according to the approximated lower and upper bounds of the state-action value function [7].   
92 SAMC. From the observation of improvement from SASC to SADC, many methods considered   
93 increasing the number of critics for improving the estimation accuracy, forming the single-actor   
94 multi-critic architecture (SAMC). Randomized ensembled double Q-learning (REDQ) [6] estimated   
95 the state-action value using the same strategy of minimum the same as TD3, yet the two critics   
96 were randomly selected from a pool of critics. REDQ also introduced a high update-to-date (UTD)   
97 ratio of 20 to address the issue of sample efficiency. For addressing the estimation accuracy issue,   
98 quasi-median Q-learning (QMQ) used the quasi-median among multiple state-action values, each   
99 of which from a critic, to estimate the state-action value, and applied on TD3, forming the QMD3.   
00 The QMD3 trained actor with delay the same as TD3, but each update is guided by all critics rather   
01 than a single one for exploration improvement. Weakly pessimistic value estimation and optimistic   
02 policy optimization (WPVOP) [17] proposed weakly pessimistic value estimation and optimistic   
03 policy optimization; the former increased and smoothed the lower confidence bound, whilst the latter   
04 encourages and increases the state-action value, as the maximum action of minimum state-action   
05 values, if the distribution of state-action values with different actions on a given state is centralized,   
06 i.e., the standard deviation less than some threshold.   
107 DADC. From single actor to double actors, double actors and regularized critics (DARC) [21] adopted   
108 double actors as well as double critics (DADC) and proposed soft target value as a linear combination   
109 of the minimum and maximum state-action values of the two actions given by two target actors, each   
110 of which is a minimum over two target critics. DARC revised the loss function adopted in TD3 by   
111 introducing a weighted regularization term of cross-critic error, i.e., the difference between the two   
112 critics.   
113 DAMC. A multi-actor mechanism (MAM) was proposed in [18]. The MAM was composed of two   
114 components, i.e., obsolescence technology (OT) and Q-value weighting technology (WT). For each   
115 actor, the OT adaptively adjust the probabilities of interacting with environment according to the   
116 accumulated reward in an episode. For each critic, the WT estimated the target of state-action value   
117 by a linear combination of state-action values achieved by the corresponding actor, and by the other   
118 actors. The MAM was integrated into TD3 (MA-TD3) with double actors and four critics, forming   
119 the double-actor multi-critic architecture (DAMC).   
120 MAMC. For multi-actor multi-critic (MAMC) architecture, the MAM was also integrated into   
121 DDPG (MA-DDPG) with three actors and three critics, which became another MAMC-based method   
122 [18]. An early MAMC method is the Simple UNified framework for ReInforcement learning using   
123 enSEmbles (SUNRISE) [16]. SUNRISE manipulated multiple SAC agents, each contained a pair of   
124 soft Q-function and an actor. SUNRISE integrated weighted Bellman backup, which decreases the   
125 influence from high variance transitions, and upper confidence bound (UCB) exploration [5].

145 4 MAMC

146 This study proposes a multi-actor-multi-critic architecture-based RL method: the Multi-Actor Multi  
147 Critic deep deterministic reinforcement learning (MAMC). There are three main features in the   
148 proposed MAMC, including the adoption of multiple actors and critics without predefined interaction,   
149 the quantile-based ensemble estimation, and the selection of actors as per proposed skill and creativity   
150 factors for exploration and exploitation. Table 2 provides the notation system used in this study.

184 Both factors are expectation over a mini-batch. Note that the two factors depends on all the critics as

text: 213 6 Experimental Results

This section examines the performance of the proposed MAMC method in terms of effectiveness and efficiency through experiments. Further analysis is made for showing the effectiveness of the proposed components, the sensitivity of introduced hyperparameters, and the validity of the MAMC.
6.1 Experimental Settings

The experiments are conducted on a set of five test environments chose from the well-known MuJuCo benchmark [31], including Hopper-v5, HalfCheetah-v5, Walker2d-v5, Ant-v5, and Humanoid-v5. These environments are all have continuous state and action spaces with different dimensions. Regarding the dimensionality, the difficulty of each environment can be regarded as either simple (Hopper-v5), medium (HalfCheetah-v5, Walker2d-v5), or hard (Ant-v5, Humanoid-v5). The properties of these environment can be found in the supplementary material Section A.3.

224 This study selects four state-of-the-art RL methods for performance comparison, including two with   
225 deterministic policy: TD3[9] and DARC[21], and two with stochastic policy: SAC[10], REDQ[6].   
226 Both TD3 and SAC used a single actor with two critics. REDQ also adopts a single actor but with ten   
227 critics, while DARC exploits two actors and two critics. The proposed MAMC utilizes ten actors   
228 and ten critics. An analysis on the number of actors and critics can be found in the supplementary   
229 material Section C.3. In addition, as the MAMC considers sample multiple reuse (SMR) [22], all the

text: 239 6.2 Effectiveness

Table 3 compares the Wilcoxon signed rank test for TD3 and DARC compared with the MAMC at early (100k), middle (200k), and late stage (300k). The details are provided in supplementary material Section C.1. At early stage, the MAMC achieves better quality than the two deterministic methods TD3-SMR and DARC-SMR. Comparing to the two SAC-based methods, the MAMC outperforms SAC-SMR but performs slightly worse than REDQ-SMR on the Hopper-v5 environment. At middle stage, the MAMC still betters TD3-SMR and DARC-SMR, yet the improvement becomes smaller than that at early stage. As for the two SAC-based methods, the trend on REDQ-SMR keeps, while the improvement on SAC-SMR also decreases. At late stage, the lead to TD3-SMR, DARC-SMR, and SAC-SMR further shrinks that the MAMC is slightly superior to TD3-SMR and SAC-SMR, but is comparable to DARC-SMR. The REDQ-SMR further surpasses the MAMC on Humanoid-v5 environment. These results reflect the merits of MAMC at early and middle stage, and the demerit at late stage.
6.3 Efficiency

Figure 1 draws the average return against environment steps for TD3-based and SAC-based methods by comparison with the MAMC on the five environments. Compared with TD3-based methods, the MAMC gains faster convergence on the three more complicated environments, i.e., Walker2d-v5, Ant-v5, and Humanoid-v5. Similarly, the MAMC converges faster than SAC-SMR on these three environments, yet the REDQ-SMR converges nicer than the MAMC on all except Walker2d-v5. These results validate the efficiency of the MAMC against the two deterministic method TD3-SMR and DARC-SMR, and the simpler stochastic method SAC-SMR.
6.4 Components Analysis

Table 4 lists the average and standard deviation of return for the MAMC with single-objective (MAMC-SO) and multi-objective actor selection strategies on Ant-v5 over eight trials. The MAMCSO averages the skill and creativity factors and selects the top actors by sorting for exploration. The exploitation selection mechanism for MAMC-SO and MAMC is the same. From the table, the MAMC performs better than MAMC-SO at all the three stages, which verifies the effectiveness of the proposed multi-objective actor selection mechanism.

Figure 2 plots the average return for the best (upper bound), worst (lower bound), and skilled (selected) actors in the MAMC in a specific trial on the five test environments. On HalfCheetah-v5 and Humanoid-v5, the MAMC is capable of selecting good actor approaching the upper bound, to wit, the best actor. For Hopper-v5, Walker2d-v5, and Ant-v5, the MAMC tracks the moving upper bound, and in most of the time the selected actor having quality beyond the average of upper and

6.5 Sensitivity Analysis

Figure 3 plots the estimated and ground-truth average discounted return against environment steps for MAMC with different quantile parameters $q$ on HalfCheetah-v5 and Walker2d-v5. It is obvious that the estimated value increases as $q$ increases; the best $q$ in terms of the smallest distance to ground-truth value is 0.4 for HalfCheetah-v5 and 0.3 for Walker2d-v5. However, the values are inconsistent to the best $q$ in terms of the average return, which is 0.5 for HalfCheetah-v5 and 0.2 for Walker2d-v5 (cf. Table 5). That is, the setting of quantile parameters $q$ should also considers the environmental preferences of optimism and pessimism. In general, a range between 0.2 and 0.3 is a good setting for environments which favor pessimism, and a value between 0.3 and 0.4 is nice for optimism cases; thus, a robust $q$ value may near 0.3, but the best one for a specific environment still needs to be investigated.
6.6 Validity Analysis

The proposed MAMC is based on deterministic policy, and the results have shown that the MAMC can ameliorate the performance of TD3-SMR and REDQ-SMR. The MAMC is also beneficial in comparison to SAC-SMR, a simple but powerful method with stochastic policy. Past studies have discovered the potential of stochastic policy over deterministic policy, and this may be the weakness of the MAMC, which is considered as the main reason to be surpassed by REDQ-SMR.
91 7 Conclusions

This study proposes a multi-actor multi-critic deep deterministic reinforcement learning method. The MAMC includes a selection of actors for exploration using skill and creativity factors, an ensemble target value based on a predefined quantile parameter, and a selection of best actor regarding skill factor for exploitation. Theoretical analysis proves the MAMC having bounded estimation error, and learning stability over SAMC and MASC. From experimental results, the MAMC excels TD3-SMR, DARC-SMR, and SAC-SMR with better quality and faster convergence on the selected environments in MuJoCo. The validity analysis shows a weakness of deterministic based method and is also a possible future extension. Another promising orientation for future research is to adapt the quantile parameter to address the issue of estimation accuracy by balancing optimism and pessimism.
